outcome: incidence of non-D Rh alloimmunized pregnancies
critical titer (> 16) from non-D Rh antibodies
cohort: All pregnancies managed at the Royal Women's Hospital, Victoria, Australia, from 2009 to 2013 inclusive
finding: Non-D Rh alloimmunization is a relatively uncommon complication of pregnancy but can lead to significant fetal/neonatal morbidity (and may lead to mortality), with the most severe outcomes associated with the compound antibodies anti-CD and anti-cE, or a non-D Rh antibody in conjunction with anti-D.
